To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single pressure image of a fingerpad does not contain enough information to estimate the surface properties of an object, that active observation of the object is necessary to obtain a stable estimate of surface properties, and that the finger-pad can be actively controlled to fix its high resolution area on the surface of an object.

(1) a single pressure image does not provide a unique estimate of the surface properties; (2) active observation of the surface is necessary to obtain a unique estimate; (3) a single pressure sensor is sufficient for active observation; (4) active control of the finger-pad is necessary to fix its high resolution region on the contact surface; (5) a simple algorithm is proposed for this active control.

a) active haptic perception is essential to achieve high accuracy in the perception of surface properties of the contact environment, and that b) the active haptic perception can be realized by a computational model of the haptic perception and the haptic servoing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational theory and algorithms for the active haptic perception and its control.
the active control of haptic perception and the computational aspects of the control.
the problem of how to actively control the fixation of haptic information during general motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
haptic perception and its control are active processes.
the active haptic perception and its control is a well-posed problem, but the problem is computationally intensive.
the problem of controlling the haptic perception of hardness and curvature is a well-posed problem, and a haptic servo system can be designed to control it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a computational framework for the haptic servoing and perception, which has the potential to be applied to a wide range of haptic perception tasks.
the haptic perception of hardness and curvation of the environment is well-posed if the finger-pad is active.
the active perception and control of the haptic perception is essential to realize the high resolution of haptic perception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
haptic perception is an active process and it is possible to actively fix the region of interest in the contact surface.
active perception is a necessary component of haptic perception, and it is possible to achieve active haptic perception and servoing using the same computational framework.
haptic perception can be controlled by active observation and control of its own fixation.
